name: Agag
overview: Agag was a male king of the Amalekites, a people descended from Amalek. His role as king is specifically noted in 1 Samuel 15:8, highlighting his leadership over this enemy nation of Israel. There is no additional tribal affiliation or personal notes recorded about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Agag likely means 'violent,' reflecting perhaps the nature or reputation of this individual. He is also identified by the title 'King of the Amalekites,' which directly states his royal authority over the Amalekite people. Neither name was given by God but are descriptive and historical identifiers.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Agag was a descendant of Amalek, linking him to the founding ancestor of the Amalekite nation. It is also inferred that he descended from Hammedatha, as noted in Esther 3:1, though this is an indirect connection. Beyond these, no further family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Agag's significance lies in his position as the Amalekite king during a key conflict with Israel, representing the ongoing enmity between Israel and Amalek. His defeat and interactions with Israelite leaders illustrate God's judgment against Amalek as an enemy of His people. Agag embodies the opposition to God's covenant community, serving as a symbol of the spiritual and physical battles faced by Israel.
